title: Existing unit test test_min_instances asserts min_instances == 1 and now fails
evidence:
tests/unit/test_concurrency.py lines 38-43:
    def test_min_instances(self) -> None:
        # min_instances = 1 keeps one warm instance so Gleam's
        # `session_create` POST never lands on a cold start. Bumped 0→1 in
        # commit 9816019 after staging cold-start failures on 2026-05-04.
        prod_tfvars = PRODUCTION_TFVARS.read_text()
        assert _extract_literal_int(prod_tfvars, "min_instances") == 1

Executed `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_concurrency.py -x -q` against this tree:
FAILED tests/unit/test_concurrency.py::TestProductionTfvarsScaling::test_min_instances
E       assert 0 == 1
 +  where 0 = _extract_literal_int('environment  = "production"\n...\ncpu_idle      = true\nmin_instances = 0\nmax_instances = 20\n', 'min_instances')
detail: Diff sets min_instances = 0 but leaves the test asserting 1, so documented `uv run pytest` fails. Worse, CI won't catch it here: pr-checks.yml paths exclude deployment/**, so it breaks the next unrelated PR.
recommended_fix: In this PR, update test_min_instances to assert 0 and rewrite its comment (cold-start tradeoff accepted, see variables.tf history); optionally assert cpu_idle = true.

title: Acceptance 'terraform fmt -check clean' fails on pre-existing staging.tfvars misalignment
evidence:
Executed `terraform fmt -check -recursive -diff` in deployment/terraform (exit 3):
vars/staging.tfvars
-cpu           = "1"
+cpu = "1"

staging.tfvars is byte-identical to develop (`git diff develop -- deployment/terraform/vars/staging.tfvars` empty), so pre-existing, not introduced by this diff. production.tfvars itself is clean (`terraform fmt -check vars/production.tfvars` exit 0).
detail: Spec acceptance #2 requires `terraform fmt -check` clean; repo state fails via a one-line pre-existing alignment issue. Repo rule 'No tech debt. Fix issues as you find them' applies.
recommended_fix: Run `terraform fmt` on deployment/terraform (fixes staging.tfvars `cpu = "1"` alignment) and include it in this PR, or explicitly note the pre-existing failure.

title: Merging is inert: no workflow runs terraform, so scale-to-zero lands only after manual tf-apply-prod
evidence:
Makefile lines 105-108, 132-134:
# Cloud Run service config (timeout, scaling, env vars, secrets) is owned by
# Terraform — see deployment/README.md. CI only pushes the container image;
# config changes require a manual `terraform apply`.
...
# Apply against production
tf-apply-prod:
	cd $(TF_DIR) && \
	  terraform init -reconfigure -backend-config="bucket=righttenantry-tf-state" && \
	  terraform apply -var-file=vars/production.tfvars

deploy-to-prod.yml push trigger paths: tenant_scorer/**, tests/**, pyproject.toml, uv.lock, Makefile, Dockerfile, main.py, .github/workflows/** — deployment/** absent; its only deploy step is `gcloud run deploy --source .`.
detail: The changed tfvars never auto-applies: deploy-to-prod.yml neither triggers on deployment/** nor runs terraform. Prod scale-to-zero takes effect only after an operator runs `make tf-apply-prod`.
recommended_fix: State in the PR body: merge alone changes nothing; someone must run `make tf-apply-prod` for production scale-to-zero to take effect.
